scope.frame: the SU(2) character variety of the once-punctured torus's free group, with the four central twists
scope.object: the rule a -> ab, b -> a and the moves L, R
scope.hypotheses: a lift exists where the character is fixed up to a central twist; stabilisers of other mapping classes (finite orbits) not computed

claim_one_line: THE RULE'S LIFTS (P-225; no data): on the SU(2) character variety the rule a -> ab, b -> a acts as the Fibonacci trace map (x, y, z) -> (z, x, xz - y) and fixes, up to each of the four central twists, only the common point (0, 0, 0) and one central character; every point fixed by two of the rule, L and R (each with any twist) is the common point or one of the four central characters (+-2, +-2, +-2), so the rule and the moves lift to SU(2) with a determined element only at the common point (at the central characters every element intertwines). There the rule's lifts have orders 3 and 6 and rotate about the (+-1, +-1, +-1) axes, and their eigenvectors are exactly the T-type magic states (Bloch vectors (+-1, +-1, +-1)/sqrt 3). Off the common point these three moves give no gate set; stabilisers of other mapping classes are not computed; the universal Fibonacci braiding lives in the level-3 quantum representation (on record, B218, B254; not selected, B24). 0 of 19.
